Theorem B's sign flip 1-6p(1-p)<=0 for |Z|<=4, A(p), B(p), quartic transition at p*=1/8, and Theorem C's KKT matching k=1/(2(|Z|-1)) and lambda=|Z|/(2(|Z|-1)) all check out cleanly.

novelty.basis: Theorem A establishes the genuinely new sharp constant 25/16 between err_hq and err_sq for non-commuting PSD operators, completing the (25/16, 4/3, 2) triangle. Theorems B and C are incremental finite-alphabet sharpenings (+50% peak at |Z|=4,5; 2-universal prefactor |Z|/(4(|Z|-1))) and a typo repair (1/(4|Z|) to 1/(2|Z|)) built directly on Regula and Cheng's framework [6].

reproducibility.basis: Provides an explicit blueprint of 22 Mathlib-free Lean 4.35.0 theorems (Table 1), an AST-audited exact-rational Python verifier, 16 JSON certificates (C01-C16, Table 2) including explicit F_q degree-3 4*-universal hash families, and 59 unit/forgery tests, though actual execution of external code/artifacts was not performed during this PDF-only audit.

rigor.basis: Theorem A provides a self-contained non-commuting operator proof (leaving only joint diagonalization in the sufficiency direction implicit). Theorems B and C derive exact algebraic tightenings from quoted inequalities of Regula-Cheng [6]. Table 1 transparently shows that the 22 Lean 4.35.0 lemmas formalize the scalar/polynomial/rational core rather than Hilbert-space operator theory.

significance.basis: Settles the exact universal constant linking err_hq and err_sq and strictly improves finite-alphabet one-shot privacy-amplification bounds across all |Z|>=2, including doubling the 2-universal strong-converse prefactor at |Z|=2. However, as Section 6 notes, the asymptotic error and strong-converse exponents of [6] as |Z| -> infinity remain unchanged.

potential_errors: In Section 3 (p. 2), the definition of pi_{|Z|/4}(X|E)_rho omits an explicit Hermiticity condition on M_{E,x}, although M_{E,x} = M_{E,x}^\dagger is implicitly required for M_{E,x}^4 <= M_{E,x}^2 and spectral truncation h(M) to hold as in [6, Lemma 8].

In Theorem A's equality characterization (p. 2), the 'only if' proof includes 0 in u notin {0, 3/5, 1} and parenthetically notes B|v>=0 for u>4/5, while the 'if' direction for general commuting matrices relies implicitly on joint diagonalization and additivity after verifying only the scalar case explicitly.
strengths: Theorem A proves the exact sharp constant 25/16 relating err_hq(A||B) and err_sq(A||B) for arbitrary non-commuting PSD operators A, B >= 0 via a remarkably clean functional-calculus clipping POVM phi(M_0) = min(I, 5M_0/4) and the exact identity 25/16(1-u)^2 - (1-5u/4) = (5u-3)^2/16 >= 0, together with a complete eigenspace equality characterization.

Theorem B identifies and exploits the sign change 1 - 6p(1-p) <= 0 for |Z| in {2,3,4} and the exact truncation coefficient A(p) = (3-9p+8p^2)/2, strictly improving the 4*-universal one-shot converse constant above 1/3 for every finite |Z| >= 2, reaching 1/2 (+50%) at |Z| in {4,5} and exhibiting an exact rational regime transition A(1/8) = B(1/8) = 1 proved by an explicit quartic factorization.

Theorem C retains the |Z|-1 factor dropped in Regula-Cheng [6, Lemma 19] and identifies/repairs the k = 1/(4|Z|) vs 1/(2|Z|) scaling typo on p. 40 of [6], strictly strengthening the 2-universal strong-converse prefactor to |Z|/(4(|Z|-1)) (doubling to 1/2 at |Z|=2).

Figures 1-3 and Tables 1-2 are numerically consistent across all checked rational values (e.g., C_sharp(1/2)=1/sqrt(6), C_sharp(1/3)=sqrt(2)/3, C_sharp(1/4)=C_sharp(1/5)=1/2, C_sharp(1/8)=7/16, C_sharp(1/16)=30/79, and the F_q degree-3 enumeration bounds C10-C12).
strong_novelty_candidates: Sharp non-commuting operator bound err_hq(A||B) <= (25/16) err_sq(A||B) with spectral-clipping POVM min(I, 5M_0/4) and exact equality characterization [A,B]=0, A=(3/2)B on supp(A) cap supp(B) (Theorem A).
Finite-alphabet 4*-universal one-shot converse constant C_sharp(p) > 1/3 with exact rational transition at p*=1/8 and peak 1/2 at |Z| in {4,5} (Theorem B).
summary: This 5-page manuscript audits and quantitatively sharpens three one-shot results of Regula and Cheng (arXiv:2611.33270v1 [6]) on quantum hypothesis testing and universal quantum privacy amplification. Theorem A proves the globally sharp bound err_hq(A||B) <= (25/16) err_sq(A||B) for arbitrary non-commuting positive semidefinite operators via the functional-calculus POVM min(I, 5M_0/4) and characterizes equality. Theorem B sharpens the 4*-universal one-shot leftover-hash converse constant from 1/3 to C_sharp(p) = (1-p)/(2 max(A(p), sqrt(B(p)))) > 1/3 for all finite |Z| = 1/p >= 2, peaking at 1/2 for |Z| in {4,5} with an exact transition at p* = 1/8. Theorem C retains the |Z|-1 factor in Regula and Cheng's strong-converse achievability proof (Lemma 19) and corrects a factor-of-2 scaling typo (1/(4|Z|) -> 1/(2|Z|)), improving the 2-universal prefactor to |Z|/(4(|Z|-1)). All algebraic steps, identities, and numerical values in the PDF check out without material error.
weaknesses: The Abstract's phrase 'complete machine-checked constructive formalization' somewhat overstates the Lean 4.35.0 kernel scope: as Table 1 transparently shows, the 22 Mathlib-free Lean theorems formalize the scalar, rational, and polynomial identities/inequalities rather than the Hilbert-space functional calculus, Loewner order, or Haagerup-Musat operator truncation steps.

The starting inequalities for Theorems B and C—specifically [6, Eqs. (118), (121), (125)] and [6, Eqs. (170)-(177)]—are cited from the concurrent preprint [6] rather than derived self-containedly in this manuscript; in particular, the manuscript's remark about dropping -p/4 in [6, Eq. (107)] cannot be verified from the PDF alone without inspecting [6].
The quantitative gains in Theorems B and C vanish asymptotically as |Z| -> infinity, leaving the optimal asymptotic one-shot converse constant beyond 1/3 open as acknowledged in Section 6.
